title: The Benefits of Walking
body: Walking is one of the simplest and most effective forms of exercise. You do not need any special equipment or a gym membership — just a comfortable pair of shoes. Studies show that walking for thirty minutes a day can improve heart health, lower blood pressure, and help with weight management. It is also great for mental health. Many people find that a short walk helps them feel less stressed and more relaxed. Walking outdoors, especially in nature, can boost your mood and improve your sleep. Doctors recommend walking as a safe activity for people of all ages. Whether you walk to work, around your neighbourhood, or in a park, the benefits are clear. Even a short daily walk can make a big difference to your overall well-being.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Walking is good for your health
Walking is dangerous for older people
questions.answer: Walking is good for your health
questions.explanation: The passage describes several physical and mental health benefits of walking.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, you need special equipment to start walking for exercise.
questions.explanation: The passage states that you do not need special equipment — just comfortable shoes.

questions.prompt: How long does the passage suggest walking each day?
questions.explanation: The passage says 'walking for thirty minutes a day' can improve health.

title: How to Save Money on Groceries
body: Buying food is one of the biggest monthly expenses for most families. However, there are several simple strategies that can help you spend less at the supermarket. First, always make a shopping list before you go. This helps you avoid buying things you do not need. Second, try to buy seasonal fruits and vegetables. They are usually fresher and cheaper than out-of-season produce. Third, compare prices between different brands. Store-brand products are often just as good as famous brands but cost much less. Another useful tip is to plan your meals for the week. When you know what you are going to cook, you buy only what you need, which reduces food waste. Finally, try not to shop when you are hungry. Studies show that hungry shoppers tend to buy more snacks and processed food. With a little planning, you can eat well and still save money every month.

questions.prompt: What is the first tip the passage gives for saving money?
questions.explanation: The passage says 'First, always make a shopping list before you go.'

questions.prompt: Store-brand products are usually worse quality than famous brands.
questions.explanation: The passage says store-brand products are 'often just as good as famous brands.'

questions.prompt: Why does the passage suggest not shopping when hungry?
options: Because you will forget your list
Because you tend to buy more snacks and processed food
Because food looks less fresh when you are hungry
questions.answer: Because you tend to buy more snacks and processed food
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'hungry shoppers tend to buy more snacks and processed food.'

questions.prompt: Planning meals for the week can help reduce food waste.
questions.explanation: The passage says that knowing what you will cook means 'you buy only what you need, which reduces food waste.'

title: The Rise of Remote Work
body:
The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically changed the way millions of people work. Before 2020, remote work was available mainly to freelancers and workers in the technology sector. However, when lockdowns forced offices to close, companies around the world had to adapt quickly. Employees set up home offices, learned to use video conferencing tools, and discovered that many tasks could be completed just as effectively outside a traditional office.

Now, several years later, remote and hybrid work models have become a permanent feature of the modern workplace. Surveys consistently show that a majority of workers prefer having the option to work from home at least part of the time. They cite benefits such as avoiding long commutes, having a more flexible schedule, and achieving a better work-life balance. Employers, too, have found advantages, including reduced office costs and access to a wider talent pool.

Nevertheless, remote work is not without challenges. Some employees report feeling isolated or struggling to separate their personal and professional lives. Managers sometimes find it harder to build team culture and monitor productivity. As organisations continue to refine their approach, the key challenge is creating a system that balances flexibility with collaboration and accountability.

questions.explanation: The passage says 'The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically changed the way millions of people work.'

questions.prompt: Before 2020, remote work was common in most industries.
questions.explanation: The passage states that remote work was previously 'available mainly to freelancers and workers in the technology sector.'

questions.explanation: The passage mentions commutes, flexibility, and work-life balance as benefits, but does not mention higher salary.

questions.explanation: The passage says 'Managers sometimes find it harder to build team culture and monitor productivity.'

title: The Ocean's Plastic Problem
body:
Every year, approximately eight million tonnes of plastic waste enter the world's oceans. This staggering figure has led scientists to warn that, by 2050, there could be more plastic in the sea than fish by weight. The problem is not limited to large, visible items such as bottles and bags. Microplastics — tiny fragments less than five millimetres in size — have been found in the deepest ocean trenches, in Arctic ice, and even in the food we eat.

The consequences for marine ecosystems are severe. Sea turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish, while seabirds often feed plastic fragments to their young. Fish that ingest microplastics can pass harmful chemicals up the food chain, ultimately reaching human plates. Coral reefs, already threatened by rising water temperatures, suffer additional damage when plastic debris smothers them and blocks sunlight.

Addressing this crisis requires action on multiple fronts. Governments can implement bans on single-use plastics and invest in waste management infrastructure. Companies should redesign products and packaging to be recyclable or compostable. Individuals, meanwhile, can reduce their plastic consumption by choosing reusable alternatives. International cooperation is also essential, as ocean currents carry plastic pollution across borders. Without coordinated effort, the health of our oceans — and our own health — will continue to decline.

options: Fish that eat them pass harmful chemicals up the food chain
questions.answer: Fish that eat them pass harmful chemicals up the food chain

questions.answer: Because ocean currents carry plastic pollution across borders
questions.explanation: The passage states 'ocean currents carry plastic pollution across borders,' making international cooperation essential.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education
body:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming the field of education, offering both remarkable opportunities and significant challenges. AI-powered tools are now capable of personalising the learning experience in ways that were previously unimaginable. Adaptive learning platforms analyse a student's strengths and weaknesses in real time, adjusting the difficulty of exercises and recommending resources tailored to individual needs. Language learning applications use speech recognition to provide instant feedback on pronunciation, while AI tutors can answer questions and explain concepts around the clock.

The potential benefits are considerable. Students in under-resourced schools, who might otherwise lack access to qualified teachers in every subject, can use AI tools to supplement their education. Teachers, freed from repetitive tasks such as grading multiple-choice tests, can devote more time to mentoring students and designing creative lessons. Furthermore, data collected by AI systems can help educators identify students who are falling behind before they reach a crisis point.

However, the integration of AI into education raises important ethical questions. There are legitimate concerns about data privacy, particularly when platforms collect detailed information about children's learning habits and behaviours. Critics also worry that an over-reliance on technology could diminish the human connection between teachers and students, which many researchers regard as fundamental to effective learning. The risk of algorithmic bias is another pressing issue; if the data used to train AI systems reflects existing inequalities, the technology may inadvertently reinforce rather than reduce educational disparities.

As schools and universities continue to experiment with AI, it is essential that policymakers establish clear guidelines to ensure that these powerful tools are used responsibly. The goal should not be to replace teachers but to empower them, creating a learning environment that combines the efficiency of technology with the empathy and insight that only a human educator can provide.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of adaptive learning platforms?
options: To personalise learning based on individual student needs
To make all students learn at the same pace
To reduce the number of subjects taught
questions.answer: To personalise learning based on individual student needs

options: By replacing them in the classroom
By freeing them from repetitive tasks like grading
questions.answer: By freeing them from repetitive tasks like grading
questions.explanation: The passage states that teachers 'freed from repetitive tasks such as grading multiple-choice tests, can devote more time to mentoring students.'

title: The Science of Habits
body:
Much of our daily behavior is governed by automatic routines known as habits. Neuroscientists explain that the brain creates habits through a three-part process: a cue, a routine, and a reward. The cue triggers the brain into automatic mode, determining which habit to use. The routine is the physical, mental, or emotional behavior that follows. Finally, the reward satisfies a craving and helps the brain remember whether this particular loop is worth storing for future use.

Over time, this loop becomes increasingly automated within the basal ganglia, an ancient region of the brain. When a habit takes hold, the brain expends less conscious energy on decision-making, allowing attention to be directed elsewhere. While this efficiency is advantageous for positive behaviors such as brushing teeth or exercising, it also explains why undesirable habits are notoriously difficult to eliminate. Trying to extinguish a habit solely through willpower often fails because the neurological craving remains intact.

Modern behavioral psychologists suggest that rather than attempting to eradicate a bad habit, one should focus on transforming the routine while keeping the cue and reward consistent. For example, if stress at work prompts you to eat sugary snacks, substituting a brisk five-minute walk can provide a similar mental reset without the negative health consequences. Furthermore, creating clear implementation intentions—such as deciding in advance exactly when and where you will practice a new behavior—dramatically increases the likelihood of long-term success.

options: A cue, a routine, and a reward
questions.answer: A cue, a routine, and a reward
questions.explanation: The passage clearly identifies the three-part process: 'a cue, a routine, and a reward.'

questions.prompt: Which brain structure is primarily involved in automating habits?
questions.explanation: The text states that the habit loop 'becomes increasingly automated within the basal ganglia.'

questions.prompt: The passage claims that willpower alone is usually sufficient to eliminate bad habits.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Trying to extinguish a habit solely through willpower often fails because the neurological craving remains intact.'

questions.prompt: What strategy does the passage recommend for changing an undesirable habit?
options: Eliminating all cues from your life
Changing the routine while preserving the cue and reward
Stopping the behavior immediately without substitutes
questions.answer: Changing the routine while preserving the cue and reward
questions.explanation: Psychologists advise 'transforming the routine while keeping the cue and reward consistent.'

title: The Architecture of Renewable Energy
body:
Transitioning global power generation from fossil fuels to sustainable sources represents one of the greatest engineering undertakings in human history. Solar and wind technologies have made enormous strides over the past decade, with costs falling by more than eighty percent in many regions. However, integrating these renewable sources into electrical grids presents unprecedented engineering challenges.

The most formidable obstacle is intermittency. Sunlight varies with cloud cover and nightfall, while wind fluctuates unpredictably. Traditional grids were engineered around steady, dispatchable power plants that could ramp production up or down on demand. To accommodate fluctuating clean energy, modern energy architects are designing intelligent grids equipped with advanced battery storage systems and bidirectional power distribution.

Utility-scale lithium-ion and flow batteries can store surplus energy generated during windy nights or sunny afternoons, releasing it during peak evening demand. Additionally, smart meters and AI-driven forecasting algorithms enable grid operators to predict consumption patterns hours in advance. Interconnecting national power grids across geographical borders also allows countries experiencing excess solar generation to export electricity to neighboring regions experiencing overcast skies. Through this combination of storage, smart distribution, and regional cooperation, a fully decarbonized energy network is becoming a viable reality.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The most formidable obstacle is intermittency. Sunlight varies with cloud cover and nightfall, while wind fluctuates unpredictably.'

questions.answer: It allows regions with excess generation to export to regions in need
questions.explanation: Interconnecting grids allows 'countries experiencing excess solar generation to export electricity to neighboring regions experiencing overcast skies.'

title: Bioluminescence: Cold Light in the Ocean
body:
In the perpetual darkness of the deep ocean, countless organisms possess the extraordinary ability to produce their own light—a phenomenon known as bioluminescence. Unlike light emitted by a lamp, which generates considerable thermal energy, bioluminescence is 'cold light,' meaning that nearly ninety percent of the energy involved is converted directly into visible illumination rather than wasted as heat.

The chemical mechanism relies on two essential substances: a light-emitting pigment called luciferin, and an enzyme designated as luciferase. When luciferase catalyzes the oxidation of luciferin, a burst of blue-green light is generated. This specific hue travels farther through oceanic depths than red or orange light, maximizing visibility in the aquatic twilight.

Marine species employ bioluminescence for diverse evolutionary purposes. Predators such as anglerfish use luminous lures dangling before their jaws to draw curious prey into striking range. Conversely, other creatures utilize luminescence for defensive deception. Many deep-sea squid expel clouds of glowing ink to dazzle and disorient attackers while they escape into the dark. Furthermore, bioluminescent research has proved invaluable to modern medicine; green fluorescent proteins extracted from luminous organisms are now standard laboratory markers used to track gene expression and observe cellular development in real time.

questions.prompt: Why is bioluminescence referred to as 'cold light'?
options: It can only occur in icy ocean waters
Most of the energy is converted into light rather than heat
It causes organisms to drop in temperature
questions.answer: Most of the energy is converted into light rather than heat
questions.explanation: The passage explains that 'nearly ninety percent of the energy involved is converted directly into visible illumination rather than wasted as heat.'

questions.prompt: Which enzyme catalyzes the chemical reaction that produces marine light?
questions.explanation: The text specifies that 'an enzyme designated as luciferase' catalyzes the oxidation of luciferin.

questions.prompt: Why is blue-green light particularly effective underwater?
options: It travels farther through ocean water than other colors
It reflects off of coral reefs
questions.answer: It travels farther through ocean water than other colors
questions.explanation: The text states that blue-green light 'travels farther through oceanic depths than red or orange light, maximizing visibility.'

questions.prompt: How has bioluminescent research contributed to modern medical science?
options: By providing a cure for common colds
By serving as fluorescent markers to track cellular development
questions.answer: By serving as fluorescent markers to track cellular development
questions.explanation: Proteins from luminous organisms 'are now standard laboratory markers used to track gene expression and observe cellular development in real time.'
